extraction_notes.note: Theorem 1 is argued in running text interrupted by Remarks 1 and 2; the argument is split into two proof parts around the remarks, the second with a uses edge to the first. The definition of primary/secondary scales inside the argument is kept as a step.

Theorem 2 only 'summarises' Section 4; the proof node starts at the paragraph applying the multiplicative model to a Cantor set, and the earlier derivation of the infinite-product solutions is kept as remarks.
remark or claim: the dimension log_3 2 and thickness 1 of the fluctuating s-sets are paper results but are argued and concluded inside one paragraph each with no separately stated claim.

The valuated exponent for s-sets is introduced inside a derived statement ('where rho ... is the valuated exponent'); split into a definition of v_R(x) and a claim carrying rho, proved by the following paragraphs.

Section 1.1 (Main Results) restates Theorems 1-3 and Proposition 2 in prose; no separate nodes were made for these previews. The 'regular metric' sentence of the introduction and the homogeneous/uniform terminology of Sec. 2 are not used later and got no node.
Solomyak's theorem on arithmetic sums of Cantor sets is only applied inside a sentence of the argument for Theorem 3, so it has no external node.

{\bf Remark 1}: 
As remarked already, the set of infinitesimals $O_{\inf} =\Phi$ when $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$. However, the corresponding asymptotic expression for the scale free (invariant) infinitesimals  is  nontrivial, in the sense that the associated valuations (\ref{eq5}) can be shown to exist as finite real numbers. 

Choosing $\epsilon=\beta^r$, the Cantor set scale factor,  the scale free infinitesimal gaps can be identified as $\tilde O^m_{\rm inf}= (0, \beta^m)$ when $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$ is realised as $n\rightarrow \infty$, $r=n+m, \ m=1,2,\ldots$. Assign nonzero constant valuation $|\tilde x_m|_u=\alpha_m$ $\forall\ \tilde X_m= \tilde x_m/\epsilon\in \tilde O^m _{\inf}$.
